title: Cleanse CI lint profiles and inline lightweight toolcache index to reduce presubmit overhead
author: Ayesha Patel
body:
Summary: Reduce presubmit latency and flakiness by pruning obsolete lint profiles, consolidating language-specific quick-check rules, and replacing the external toolcache index lookup with an inlined, memory-light index used only at bootstrap. Motivation: Over the last 6 months presubmit median setup time regressed (~18s) due to repeated remote toolcache lookups and profile expansion for small changes. This PR reduces I/O during CI init and shrinks the lint profile surface so fastpath changes (docs/README or small TS fixes) skip heavy lint shards.

What I changed (high level):
- Consolidated 9 legacy lint profile YAMLs into 3 staged profiles (fast, standard, full) and introduced a compact selector that uses path globs to map files to shards.
- Inlined a tiny toolcache index implementation (scripts/toolcache/index_inline.go) that replaces remote HTTP lookup for common tool versions during CI bootstrap; it lives inside the CI runner image and falls back to the old fetcher only if an entry is missing.
- Updated presubmit composite workflow (.github/workflows/presubmit.yml) to prefer the new compact profiles for pre-merge quick checks and route longtests to the nightly lane.
- Added docs/ci/migration-clean-profiles.md with instructions for teams to opt into fast/standard profiles and guidance for adding exceptions.

Why this is safe: The index is additive and scoped to the CI bootstrap path; runtime serving code is unaffected. Lint behavior is preserved for the full profile; fast/standard merely toggle which plugins/shards run. All changes are opt-in by default for long-running jobs (nightly).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind a feature gate in the presubmit composite (this PR flips the gate to enabled for the org).
2) Monitor presubmit median setup and queue time for 48hrs.
3) If regressions appear, revert the gate and roll back the index (fallback path is still available).

Migration notes for integrators:
- Teams using custom lint profiles: copy your overrides into .ci/teams/<team>/profile.yaml and add an entry to docs/ci/custom-profiles.md (examples included).
- If your toolchain depends on an obscure tool version not present in the inlined index, CI will fetch it from the cache server transparently; open SUP-3456 if you need a persistent addition.

Testing performed:
- Local shim integration run (make ci-bootstrap) on Mac and Linux containers.
- Full presubmit run triggered on this branch: see ci checks below.
- Canary rollout: enabled for infra/* and docs/* paths for 24h before full flip.

Performance expectations:
- Expected median presubmit bootstrap time reduced by ~12–16s on average (measured in staging runners).
- CI cache hit rate for toolchain fetches improved from 71% to 93% in staged tests.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: missing tool version in index -> mitigation: transparent fetch fallback and rapid add via SUP-3456.
- Risk: teams depend on shard ordering -> mitigation: documented profiles and a stable full profile that is unchanged semantically.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added for index loader [x] integration smoke for presubmit [x] docs updated [x] Linear tickets linked

Commits summary: see commits field.

Files of interest: see files_changed.

refactor(toolcache): add inlined index with transparent fallback to remote fetcher
chore(ci): route fast profile to presubmit quicklane; nightly for full checks
test(ci): add unit tests for inline index loader and selector mapping
docs(ci): add migration guide and team override examples
